note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Apply a late penalty to an assignment score. The score loses 10% of the maximum points for each started 24-hour period after the deadline, for up to 5 periods. Work submitted more than 5 periods late scores 0. A score never goes below 0. Work submitted at or before the deadline is not penalised.
facts: Made-up examples, maximum 50 points, raw score 45: submitted 1 hour late, 1 period, score 40. Submitted 49 hours late, 3 periods, score 30. Submitted 120 hours and 1 minute late, 6 periods, score 0.

route.text:

Decision: the full panel. Two independent models check each other, and a person signs off at every gate.
A low-risk request, such as fixing a typo, would go to one model and a person, at a fraction of the cost.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1: Work submitted at or before the deadline keeps its raw score with no penalty.
REQ-2: Lateness is counted in started 24-hour periods after the deadline. Any part of a period counts as a full period, so 1 minute to 24 hours is 1 period and just over 24 hours is 2 periods.
REQ-3: For 1 to 5 periods late, the penalty is 10% of the maximum points per period, subtracted from the raw score.
REQ-4: Work submitted more than 5 periods late (more than 120 hours) scores 0, and a penalised score never goes below 0.
AC-1: Maximum 50, raw score 45, submitted 1 hour late: 1 period, penalty 5, score 40.
AC-2: Maximum 50, raw score 45, submitted 49 hours late: 3 periods, penalty 15, score 30.
AC-3: Maximum 50, raw score 45, submitted 120 hours and 1 minute late: 6 periods, which is more than 5, so score 0.
AC-4: Maximum 50, raw score 45, submitted exactly at the deadline: score 45. Maximum 50, raw score 3, submitted 1 hour late: 3 minus 5 would be -2, so score 0 (illustrative case derived from the brief's rules).
panel.draftB:
REQ-1: Work submitted at or before the deadline is not penalised and keeps its raw score.
REQ-2: Deduct 10% of the maximum points from the raw score for each started 24-hour period after the deadline, for up to 5 periods.
REQ-3: A period counts once any time in it has passed, so an exact multiple of 24 hours does not start the next period.
REQ-4: Work more than 5 periods late scores 0, and the resulting score never goes below 0.
AC-1: Maximum 50, raw score 45, submitted 1 hour late: 1 period, deduct 5, score 40.
AC-2: Maximum 50, raw score 45, submitted 49 hours late: 3 periods, deduct 15, score 30.
AC-3: Maximum 50, raw score 45, submitted 120 hours and 1 minute late: 6 periods, score 0.

reviewOfA.strengths: Every stated threshold and example recomputes correctly, including 1 hour to 40, 49 hours as 3 periods to 30, and 120 hours 1 minute as 6 periods scoring 0 rather than a continued deduction.

findings.title: Boundary rule not in brief
findings.detail: The brief and facts do not say whether exactly 24, 48 or 120 hours late starts the next period. REQ-3 settles this boundary as a new rule. The requester should confirm it before approval or mark it as an assumption, since it decides 0 versus a positive score at 120 hours.
findings.quote: so an exact multiple of 24 hours does not start the next period.

findings.title: Edge cases lack acceptance criteria
findings.detail: No AC covers on-time submission, an exact 24-hour boundary, or the zero floor. One example would be raw 10, maximum 50, 3 periods late, giving 0 rather than -5. Adding these cases would make REQ-1, REQ-3 and REQ-4 testable.
findings.quote: REQ-4: Work more than 5 periods late scores 0, and the resulting score never goes below 0.

reviewOfB.strengths: All three acceptance criteria correctly reproduce the given examples: deductions of 5 and 15 points and scores of 40, 30 and 0.

merge.document:
REQ-1: Work submitted at or before the deadline is not penalised and keeps its raw score.
REQ-2: Lateness is counted in started 24-hour periods after the deadline. Any part of a period counts as a full period.
REQ-3: For 1 to 5 periods late, deduct 10% of the maximum points per period from the raw score.
REQ-4: Work more than 5 periods late scores 0, and a penalised score never goes below 0.
REQ-5 (assumption, requester to confirm): A submission exactly 24, 48, 72, 96 or 120 hours late does not start the next period. So exactly 120 hours late is 5 periods, not 6. The brief does not settle this.
AC-1: Maximum 50, raw score 45, submitted 1 hour late: 1 period, deduct 5, score 40.
AC-2: Maximum 50, raw score 45, submitted 49 hours late: 3 periods, deduct 15, score 30.
AC-3: Maximum 50, raw score 45, submitted 120 hours and 1 minute late: 6 periods, which is more than 5, so score 0.
AC-4: Maximum 50, raw score 45, submitted exactly at the deadline: score 45.
AC-5: Maximum 50, raw score 10, submitted 3 periods late: 10 minus 15 would be -5, so score 0. This is an illustrative case derived from the brief's rules.
AC-6 (depends on REQ-5): Maximum 50, raw score 45, submitted exactly 120 hours late: 5 periods, deduct 25, score 20.
merge.keptFromA: From draft A, I kept the explicit lateness-counting rule that any part of a period counts as a full period, the separate 1-to-5-period penalty requirement, and the on-time acceptance criterion.
merge.keptFromB: From draft B, I kept the concise wording of REQ-1 and REQ-4, the 'deduct' phrasing in the acceptance criteria, and the treatment of exact 24-hour multiples, now flagged as an assumption for the requester to confirm.

resolutions.finding: D-B1 · P1 · Boundary rule not in brief
resolutions.note: REQ-5 now states the exact-multiple rule as an assumption the requester must confirm. AC-6, which depends on it, is labelled. Draft A's matching unstated boundary claim ('1 minute to 24 hours is 1 period') was removed from REQ-2.

resolutions.finding: D-B2 · P2 · Edge cases lack acceptance criteria
resolutions.note: I added AC-4 for on-time submission (score 45). I added AC-5 for the zero floor: raw 10, 3 periods late, 10-15=-5, so 0. I added AC-6 for the exact 120-hour boundary: 5 periods, 45-25=20.

finalReview.strengths: The draft correctly recomputes every given example, including 1 hour late to 40, 49 hours late to 30, and 120 hours 1 minute late to 0.

build.contract: applyLatePenalty(input) where input = { maxPoints, rawScore, deadline, submittedAt } (numbers; deadline and submittedAt are milliseconds since the Unix epoch). Returns { periodsLate: number (a whole number of started 24-hour periods; 0 when not late), deduction: number (points removed, in the same units as maxPoints), score: number (the final score) }. countLatePeriods(input) where input = { deadline, submittedAt } (numbers, milliseconds since the Unix epoch). Returns a number (a whole number of started 24-hour periods; 0 when not late). Both functions throw an Error whose message is "unknown field: <name>" if input has any other field.

architecture.draft:
Components: one pure module, latePenalty, exporting countLatePeriods and applyLatePenalty. No I/O, clock or storage; callers supply all times as epoch milliseconds.
countLatePeriods({deadline, submittedAt}): reject any other field with Error "unknown field: <name>". Let diff = submittedAt - deadline. If diff <= 0, return 0 (REQ-1, AC-4). Otherwise return ceil(diff / 86400000) (REQ-2). Exact multiples do not start a new period, so exactly 120 h gives 5 (REQ-5, AC-6, pending requester confirmation).
applyLatePenalty({maxPoints, rawScore, deadline, submittedAt}): reject unknown fields. Call countLatePeriods with only {deadline, submittedAt}; passing the whole input would make it throw.
Scoring: if periods > 5, score = 0 (REQ-4). Otherwise score = max(0, rawScore - maxPoints * periods / 10). Compute as multiply then divide to avoid 0.1 float drift (REQ-3).
Assumption to confirm: deduction = rawScore - score, i.e. points actually removed after the floor at 0. This gives AC-1 deduction 5 (score 40), AC-2 15 (30), AC-3 45 (0), AC-4 0 (45), AC-5 10 (0), AC-6 25 (20). The alternative is the nominal 10% x periods.
Data: inputs are numbers only. Output is {periodsLate, deduction, score}. No persisted data, no schema change.
Not specified, so no behaviour is designed for: non-numeric or negative inputs, and rawScore above maxPoints. Flag these to the requester.
File fence (paths assumed; the repo layout was not given): src/latePenalty.js (new) and test/latePenalty.test.js (new, covering AC-1 to AC-6 plus unknown-field errors for both functions). No other files may change.
architecture.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Fixed 86400000 ms periods and ceil match every given case: 1 hour is 1 period, 49 hours is 3, exactly 120 hours is 5, and 120 hours plus 1 minute is 6, and scoring then keeps on-time raw scores, applies 10 percent per period, and floors at 0.
architecture.final:
No findings to resolve; the architecture stands as approved, and I rechecked every figure.
Components: one pure module, latePenalty, exporting countLatePeriods and applyLatePenalty. It has no I/O, clock or storage; callers pass times as epoch ms.
countLatePeriods({deadline, submittedAt}): any other field throws Error "unknown field: <name>". diff = submittedAt - deadline. If diff <= 0, return 0 (REQ-1). Otherwise return ceil(diff / 86400000) (REQ-2). So 1 h gives 1, 49 h gives 3, exactly 120 h gives 5 (REQ-5, pending confirmation) and 120 h 1 min gives 6.
applyLatePenalty({maxPoints, rawScore, deadline, submittedAt}): rejects unknown fields and calls countLatePeriods with only {deadline, submittedAt}.
Scoring: if periods > 5, score = 0. Otherwise score = max(0, rawScore - maxPoints * periods / 10), multiplying before dividing (REQ-3, REQ-4).
Assumption to confirm: deduction = rawScore - score. Results: AC-1 5/40, AC-2 15/30, AC-3 45/0, AC-4 0/45, AC-5 10/0, AC-6 25/20. The alternative is nominal 10% x periods.
Data: numeric inputs only. Output is {periodsLate, deduction, score}. No persistence or schema change.
Not specified, flagged to the requester: non-numeric or negative inputs, rawScore above maxPoints, and missing fields.
File fence (paths assumed): src/latePenalty.js and test/latePenalty.test.js, both new, with tests for AC-1 to AC-6 plus unknown-field errors for both functions. No other files change.

code.summary:
This is one pure expression that returns countLatePeriods and applyLatePenalty, built to the approved architecture. Any field outside the allowed ones throws an Error "unknown field: <name>". A non-object input also throws, which goes beyond the contract.

countLatePeriods works out diff = submittedAt - deadline. It returns 0 when diff <= 0 and ceil(diff / 86400000) otherwise. That means exactly 24, 48 or 120 hours late does not start the next period (REQ-5, still waiting on the requester to confirm).

applyLatePenalty gives a score of 0 when periodsLate > 5. Otherwise the score is max(0, rawScore - maxPoints * periods / 10), multiplying before dividing. Deduction is rawScore - score, an assumption that also needs confirming.

Checked against the examples with maximum 50:
- AC-1: raw 45, 1 h late: 1 period, deduct 5, score 40.
- AC-2: raw 45, 49 h late: 3 periods, deduct 15, score 30.
- AC-3: raw 45, 120 h 1 min late: 6 periods, deduct 45, score 0.
- AC-4: raw 45, on time: 0 periods, deduct 0, score 45.
- AC-5: raw 10, 3 periods late: score 0, deduct 10.
- AC-6: raw 45, exactly 120 h late: 5 periods, deduct 25, score 20.

Still not handled, as flagged in the architecture: non-numeric or negative inputs, rawScore above maxPoints, and missing fields. A missing deadline or submittedAt gives NaN, which the !(diff > 0) check counts as 0 periods. Unit tests are not included here.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Ceiling division by a fixed 86400000 ms counts each started 24-hour period and does not open the next period on an exact multiple, matching REQ-2, REQ-5, the zero floor, the cutoff after five periods, and AC-1 through AC-6.
code.resolutions: Review reports no defects; the module meets REQ-1 to REQ-5 and AC-1 to AC-6. applied: I checked each case independently and the code is unchanged. AC-1: 1 h late is 1 period, 45-5=40. AC-2: 49 h is ceil(49/24)=3 periods, 45-15=30. AC-3: 120 h 1 min is 6 periods, more than 5, so the score is 0. AC-4: on time is 0 periods, 45. AC-5: 10-15 is floored to 0. AC-6: exactly 120 h is 5 periods, 45-25=20, per REQ-5. Deduction is the number of points actually removed. In AC-5 that is 10, not 15, which fits the 'points removed' contract. Open items: REQ-5 is still an assumption the requester must confirm. Invalid or non-numeric inputs are not covered by the brief.
